hintRestructure.message: This can take a long time since it re-reads and re-labels every email involved (not just moving existing labels). Lets AI look at your whole label set and reorganize it: labels with overlapping meaning get grouped under a shared parent, and labels with too many different kinds of mail get split into a few clear sub-labels. Sub-labels are only kept if they'd hold a meaningful number of emails, and names are kept to a single short word. Existing sub-labels are reused instead of creating near-duplicates.

guideSubtitle.message: Gmail AI Labeler - personal OAuth client setup (assuming an account that has never used Google Cloud before, about 10 minutes)

guideWhyBox.message:
Why is this needed?
When an extension that handles Gmail data is used by "many people," Google requires a security review (once past 100 users), which can create cost/process burden for the developer. Instead, if each person uses an OAuth client issued in their own name, Google treats it as "personal development/testing use" and no review is required. It's a bit of a hassle, but you only need to do it once.

guideNoBillingBox.message: Note: The Gmail API/Drive API used by this extension are both free APIs, so they can be enabled without a billing account (card registration). If a billing-related screen appears during the steps below, it's about some other paid service unrelated to this extension - just skip it or go back.

guideStep1Title.message: Step 1. Create a Google Cloud project

guideStep1List.message:
• Create a new project in Google Cloud Console
  • If this is your first time visiting Cloud Console with this account, a "select country + accept terms of service" welcome screen may appear before the project creation screen. Check the box and click "Agree and continue" to be taken automatically to the project creation screen.
  • Any project name is fine (e.g. "gmail-labeler-personal"). Click "Create" and wait a few seconds (progress shows in the bell icon top right).
  • Once created, check that the project you just made is selected in the project dropdown at the top (click it and select manually if not).

guideStep2Title.message: Step 2. Enable Gmail API + Google Drive API

guideStep2List.message:
• Open the Gmail API library page
  • (with the project you just made selected) Click the blue "ENABLE" button. Takes a few seconds.
  • Open the Google Drive API library page
  • Click "ENABLE" here too (needed for the settings backup feature - skip if you won't use it)

guideStep2Box.message: This extension only uses the drive.file scope - it can only access the one backup file it created itself, and can't see any other files in your Drive. Under Google's policy this is a "non-sensitive" scope, so it can be used as-is without a separate security review.

guideStep3Title.message: Step 3. Configure the OAuth consent screen

guideStep3List.message:
• Open the OAuth consent screen page
  • User Type: choose External, then create
  • Enter an app name (anything, e.g. "Gmail Labeler"), user support email (your Gmail), and developer contact email (your Gmail), then save and continue
  • On the Scopes screen, just save and continue (can be skipped)
  • On the Test users screen, click "ADD USERS" to add your own Gmail address. Every account that will use this extension must be added here.
  • Save and continue → review summary → back to dashboard
  • Leave the publishing status as "Testing". Do not click "Publish to production" - that would make it subject to review.

guideStep4Title.message: Step 4. Create the OAuth Client ID (redirect URI auto-computed)

guideStep4List.message:
• Open the Credentials page
  • Click "+ Create Credentials" at the top → choose "OAuth client ID"
  • Application type: choose Web application (important - not "Desktop app")
  • Name it anything (e.g. "Gmail Labeler Extension")
  • Paste the value below into "Authorized redirect URIs" exactly as shown (this page already read your extension ID and computed it automatically - no need to visit chrome://extensions):

guideRedirectUriPlaceholder.message: https://(open this page from the extension to auto-fill).chromiumapp.org/

guideStep4List2.message: • Clicking Create shows your Client ID and Client Secret. Copy both.

guideStep4WarnBox.message: Note: You'll also see a "Chrome Extension" type in the list - don't pick that one. It can't register a custom redirect URI (doesn't match our setup) and doesn't issue a secret at all. You must pick "Web application" so the redirect URI field appears and a secret is issued normally.

guideStep4NoteBox.message: If you created a "Web application" client but still don't see a secret, click into the client's detail page from the credentials list - the "Client secret" field should have a value there (click the eye icon if it's hidden). If it's genuinely still not there, you can leave the secret field blank in the extension settings and save anyway - it will still try to connect using just the Client ID.

guideStep5Title.message: Step 5. Enter it in the extension and connect

guideStep5List.message:
• In the extension popup → Settings tab → paste the Client ID/Secret into the "Google account connection (personal OAuth)" section and save
  • Click "Connect Google account" → sign in to Google in the new window
  • If a "Google hasn't verified this app" warning appears, it's safe as long as you're signing in with the account you added as a test user in step 3 → click "Advanced" → click "Go to [app name] (unsafe)" → grant permission
  • Once connected and back in the popup, classification features will work normally.

guideStep5Box.message: If you connected before this update: the required permission scope grew when the Drive backup feature was added. Click "Disconnect" → "Connect Google account" again in the Settings tab to re-authenticate so Drive backup works properly.

guideFooterNote.message: If something's not working, double-check: (1) the account you're signing in with is added as a test user, (2) the redirect URI exactly matches the auto-computed value above (no typos/spaces), (3) the application type is "Web application".

hintBackupPassphrase.message: If you enter a passphrase here before backing up, only your API keys/OAuth secret get encrypted with it (other settings are stored as-is). You'll need to enter the same passphrase here to restore them. The passphrase itself is never stored, so if you forget it those credentials can't be recovered (you can just re-enter them manually). Leave this blank to store them in plain text as before.
